name: Qube Browser 0.1.15-alpha
notes:
Splitscreen — a FIRST version

Two pages side by side, and this is the initial cut of it: the parts below work,
the parts under Known are not built yet. Expect to find edges.

- Right-click a tab and choose Split Right to put it beside the one you are
  looking at.
- Each half carries its own compact bar: back, forward, reload, copy link, the
  domain, the page menu and a close. The bar takes the site's own colour, and
  its text is dark or light depending on which reads on it.
- While a split is open the top strip's address bar and navigation stand down.
  Every pane has its own, and two places showing the same address is one too
  many.
- The pair is one row in the sidebar, and it survives a relaunch.
- Clicking a half moves everything to that half. Ctrl+W, or the bar's close,
  shuts that pane and leaves the other as an ordinary full-width tab.
- A pinned tab or an Essential can go into a split, but always as a copy: the
  pin and the Essential's own tab are left alone.

The window, in two styles

Settings now carries Browser Style, and it changes where the address bar and the
window's buttons live.

- Mac. The page begins at the very top of the window, the strip keeps only the
  sidebar's width beside it, and the window's own buttons are three coloured
  dots at the top left. Every page carries the compact bar described above,
  split or not, so the address is always over the page it belongs to.
- Windows. The strip runs across the top with the address bar and the navigation
  in it, and Windows draws its own buttons at the right. A pane bar appears only
  once there is more than one pane to describe.

- The bar's colour is the site's own: the colour a page declares, or, for a page
  that declares none, the colour read off the top of the page itself. It is read
  as soon as anything is drawn and again once the page settles.

The Library, rebuilt after Arc

- Search covers every section now, not History alone, and the field names the
  section it is searching.
- Rows are gathered into dated runs -- Today, Yesterday, 2 weeks ago -- instead
  of each carrying a timestamp of its own.
- A row leads with what it is: the site's favicon, or the file's own icon for a
  download. Favicons come from the cache only, so opening a long history does
  not fire hundreds of requests.
- The rail is a band running the window's full height, into both corners, with
  its buttons spread evenly over it.
- Opening the Library borrows the sidebar's full width and hands it back on the
  way out. Your own width is not overwritten.
- Everything that acts on the sidebar's contents hides while the Library is
  open, and the list no longer sits on a card of its own.

Tabs

- Dropping a page above the pinned boundary keeps it; dropping it below lets it
  go. The rule the folders already used.

Downloads

- A finished download says what it is under its name: "PDF", "ZIP".

Sites

- A site is asked about before it gets the camera, the microphone or your
  location, and the answer is remembered per site, per Space.
- The page menu carries its full set of entries.

Known

- Splitscreen has no draggable divider yet. The two panes are always half and
  half.
- You cannot yet make a split by dragging a tab onto the page, nor by
  Alt-clicking a link. Right-click a tab is the only way in for now.
- A split restored from a previous session appears once you click either half.
- In Mac style the three dots close, minimise and maximise, but hovering the
  green one does not open Windows' snap-layout menu. Windows style keeps it.
- A download does not yet say which site it came from; that needs an engine
  change that is not in this build.
- An extension popup still takes about a second to appear.
summary: Splitscreen, in a first version: two pages side by side, each with its own colour-matched bar. And Settings now chooses between two window styles, Mac or Windows.
